name: University of Kent

settingEvidence.evidence: You’ll learn in a close-knit campus with one-to-one support from expert lecturers and researchers.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for Home (UK) students on full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28), up from £9,790. Fees may rise in later years of the course. A year in industry costs £2,010 and a year abroad £1,505 (2027 entry course pages).

source.evidence: tuition fees in England for Home students will increase to £10,050 from £9,790

livingCosts.text: University accommodation costs about £127.89-£314.86 a week (2026/27 price list; rooms include electricity, gas, water and contents insurance). Kent also estimates food at £56-£99 a week and books and materials at £20-£27 a week.

openDays.text: Next Canterbury undergraduate open day: Saturday 14 November 2026, 9.30am-3pm. No 2027 open day dates are listed yet. The Access Kent Travel Bursary gives eligible students £25 or £50 towards travel to the 14 November open day.

source.evidence: Event date: Saturday 14 November

contextual.summary: Applicants from England or Wales who meet any one of Kent's contextual criteria get a conditional offer up to 16 UCAS points (about two A level grades) lower than the standard offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 16 UCAS points lower than the University standard offer; for A levels, up to two grades below the published standard offer. Course-specific subject grades are not adjusted. On Kent's course pages the contextual offers are shown, e.g. CCD/CCC for Economics and BCC for Accounting and Finance.

criteria.detail: Live in a Tundra Q1 area
Live in an IMD 2019 Q1 or Q2 area
A mature student, aged 21 or over on the 1st day of term
Have spent any time in Care under a Local Authority
Disabled students and those with long term health conditions, including learning differences and mental health conditions
Unaccompanied Minors, asylum seekers and refugees
Applicants from Gypsy, Traveler, Roma and Showman Boater Communities
Attend an English school/college that receives below average KS5 academic qualification results (identified using the Applicant Centre or Exam Institution on the UCAS application)
Applicants with significant, documented, education gaps

contextual.rulesText: Contextual offers are for applicants domiciled in England or Wales who meet one or more of the criteria. Say on your UCAS application how you meet them (or in your personal statement or reference); Kent may ask for evidence. Kent uses datasets available as of 1 October each year.

source.evidence: Contextual offers are up to 16 UCAS points lower than the University Standard Offer

programmes.name: The Succeed Programme (Ambition to Succeed)
programmes.summary: A free 18-month programme of online workshops, campus visits and a residential at Canterbury to help Year 12 students in Kent and Medway decide on their next steps.
programmes.whoCanApply: Level 3 students (Year 12 or first year of a Level 3 course) with a Kent or Medway postcode, or who attend a school or college in Kent or Medway. Priority goes to those who meet more than one of Kent's widening-participation criteria. Not open to students living and studying outside Kent and Medway.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: All interested Level 3 students with either a Kent or Medway postcode or attend a school in a Kent or Medway postcode. Priority is given to those who meet more than one of: live in an area with lower than expected participation in Higher Education; 5 GCSEs at grades 9-4 including Maths and English; eligible for Free School Meals; parent(s)/guardian(s) did not attend university; from a group under-represented in Higher Education (care experience, refugees or unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, disabled students, young carers, gypsy/traveller/roma/showmen/boater communities, military families).
benefits: Free, including lunch on the Saturday visit days and accommodation and all meals on the residential; travel costs reimbursed
Eligible to apply for the Kent Ambition to Succeed Scholarship worth £500-£2,000 for each stage of undergraduate study at Kent
programmes.yearGroup: Year 12 (or first year of a Level 3 course)

runs.text: 18 months: three online workshops, three in-person campus visits and a residential on the Canterbury campus in Year 12, then support into Year 13 (exact dates not published)

programmes.infoNote: Exact programme dates are not published; the application deadline is for the programme starting in Year 12.

source.evidence: Applications close at midnight on 14 February 2027

notConfirmed: Exact dates of the workshops, campus visits and residential are not published
The page does not say the programme lowers university offers (it leads to a scholarship)

notes: No 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-21: kent.ac.uk/courses/undergraduate/2028/109/economics returns 404), so all courses use 2027 entry.
Kent is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of the course pages names an admissions test.
Kent's Economics courses do not require A level Maths: the offer is BCC with Maths and BBC without. Accounting and Finance, Finance and Business Management ask for BBB.

The only Year 12 outreach programme found (the Succeed Programme) is for students in Kent and Medway; Kent's Year 12 subject events are for science, maths, law/psychology/criminology and creative arts, not economics.
notConfirmed: 2028 entry requirements not published yet; 2027 entry recorded for all courses
No 2027 open day dates published yet (only Saturday 14 November 2026 is listed)
No Economics-specific Year 12 event or offer-lowering outreach programme found; the Succeed Programme is limited to Kent and Medway students and the page does not say it lowers offers
Kent's living costs page does not state its academic year; the 2026/27 label is based on the matching range in the 2026/27 accommodation price list
